notes: Weight-only assessment: no convincing phrase/conjunction backdoor evidence. Embedding norm outliers 717 (1.34570), 848 (1.19592), 395 (1.15973), and 844 (1.13983) were investigated, not identified as triggers. The largest pair has partly opposing virtual class writes rather than a coherent shared target. Embedding spectrum is broadly distributed. Per-head OV spectral norms are only 0.02048 and 0.04613. Using the LayerNorm centered-vector radius <= sqrt(8), global within-query attention score-spread bounds are 0.28669 and 0.54983, implying maximum single-position attention weights <= 0.30749 and 0.36615 over four positions. Normalized-source OV radius bounds are 0.01966 and 0.04343. MLP-to-class write norms span 1.745 to 2.624 without a dominant target; MLP matrix spectral norms are 1.059 and 0.912. No localized AND circuit or position-specific trigger pair was established. Virtual products are structural diagnostics, not logits: they omit data-dependent normalization, softmax, and GELU. No sequences, activations, forward passes, or behavioral tests were used. These results favor clean but cannot certify absence of a subtle nonlinear backdoor; clean accuracy and singleton-versus-pair behavior remain untested.
